use: The armoured horse of the Persian and Palmyrene heavy cavalry, mesh only: skinned in Blender to the game's own horse skeleton (scripts/assets/bind-horse.py), so its hooves stay planted, its rider seated, and formations and fallen horses work as with the code-built horse, which stays the stand-in.

generator.prompt: An armoured cavalry horse of the Sasanian Persian and Palmyrene heavy cavalry of the mid-3rd century AD, standing square for rigging: all four legs straight and vertical, evenly spaced, head raised and facing forward, tail hanging straight down, symmetrical. A tall, strong horse about 1.55 metres at the withers, grey coat with a dark mane and tail. It wears a close-fitting armour trapper of small overlapping iron scales sewn on leather, covering the neck, chest and body down to the belly, with an open space on the back where a saddle sits, like the scale horse armour found at Dura-Europos, and a plain leather bridle; the legs below the trapper are bare. Realistic proportions, anatomically accurate, worn and practical. No saddle, no saddle cloth, no rider, no face mask, no plumes, no spikes, no text or inscriptions, no modern objects, no fantasy elements.
